A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WizardMath and RLEIF, with identifiable correspondences in the methods and GSM8k/MATH experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original WizardMath benchmark results for 7B, 13B and 70B models, MATH subtopic scores, and generated solution cases in Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 reports original WizardMath benchmark results, component ablations, verifier experiments, out-of-domain evaluations and contamination analyses, including substantial appendix results.

M1.justification: V1 describes SFT on regenerated seed solutions followed by active evolution and PPO; v2 uses GPT-4-evolved problems for SFT. IRM ranking criteria change from definition, precision and integrity to difficulty and definition. V2 also introduces PRM-weighted answer aggregation at inference in Section 3.4. These substantially revise the training and inference procedures.

E1.justification: GSM8k and MATH remain, while v2 adds seven out-of-domain benchmarks: College Math, TAL, Math23k, Ape210k, GaokaoBench Math, AGIEval Gaokao Math and AGIEval SAT Math. Tables 7 and 18 extend evaluation to additional school, college and examination settings beyond v1's coverage.

E2.justification: The GSM8k/MATH comparisons drop older comparators such as Falcon, MPT and Vicuna and add MetaMath, DART-Math, Xwin-Math, MathScale, Skywork-Math and newer proprietary models. V2 also introduces reward and verification comparisons against ORM, PRM800k, Math-Shepherd and self-consistency in Tables 4–5 and Figure 3.

E3.justification: V1 reports eight evolution turns producing a 96k instruction corpus; v2 describes five-round evolution, 418k SFT examples and a separate 90k reward-training instruction set. V2 adds test-overlap filtering, multiple backbone families and scales from 0.1B to 70B, controlled data-size sweeps, and verification using 1–256 candidate solutions. Headline greedy CoT pass@1 evaluation is retained.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's subtopic breakdown and selected solution cases, v2 adds PRM/IRM ablations, upward/downward evolution ablations, data-scaling studies, reward-source comparisons, verifier sensitivity, out-of-domain testing and contamination checks. Appendix Tables 15–18 further examine synthesis methods and transfer of reward training to other SFT models. The original six solution-comparison cases are replaced with evolution and error-labeling examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent repeated-run counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. V2's multiple sampled solutions are inference budgets, not repeated experimental runs or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces WizardMath-Llama2-70B's GSM8k/MATH results of 81.6/22.7 with 92.8/58.6 under revised training conditions. V2 adds many backbone, ablation and generalization results, including Mistral-7B scores of 90.7/55.4 and PRM verification scores of 95.2/64.7 with 256 candidates in Table 5. These are not controlled same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: V2 adds explicit mathematical definitions for IRM ranking loss, PRM step-label loss and PRM-weighted answer aggregation in Equations 1, 2 and 4. V1 specifies only the combined reward product. This is a limited addition of formal methodological definitions; no theoretical guarantees or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The central contribution broadens from improving Llama-2 to improving multiple backbone families, with new claims about data efficiency and the importance of instruction evolution and process supervision. V1 acknowledges trailing GPT-4 and Claude 2; v2 claims superiority over early GPT-4 and other proprietary models and emphasizes strong performance from a 7B Mistral model.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations concerning complementary evolution directions, instruction-quality control, PRM's advantages on longer reasoning problems, and generalization across backbones and datasets. It attributes gains to evolved-data quality rather than contamination and discusses the accuracy-cost tradeoff of replacing GPT-4 with an open teacher. Appendix A.7 also explains DART-Math's advantage at small data scales.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendices A.1–A.5 add model-version information, learning rates, epoch counts, batch size, sequence length, data-construction details, and evolution, ranking, labeling and filtering prompts. Minimum-over-steps PRM reward aggregation is newly documented. V1's literal training/evaluation templates and explicit Hugging Face access pointer are omitted; this does not establish that resources became unavailable.

R1.justification: V2 substantially updates positioning around mathematical data synthesis, modern math-specialized models and process supervision, adding discussion of MetaMath, DART-Math, Xwin-Math, Llemma and other newer work. It explicitly distinguishes its approach from Python-assisted reasoning and human-labeled supervision. V1's broad instruction-fine-tuning survey is removed.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction and results narrative, moves related work before the method, and reorganizes method and experimental sections. The two-part solution-case appendix becomes a ten-part prompt and analysis appendix. Citation style, authorship and affiliations also change.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, the original GSM8k leaderboard bar chart disappears, and new scaling, verification and similarity plots appear. Table 1 gains a backbone column and extensive grouping. Compact ablation tables and color-coded annotation cases replace the original long solution tables, with substantial changes to figure/table placement and surrounding layout.

improvement.justification: V1 mainly supports its method through benchmark scores and selected solutions. V2 adds direct component ablations, stronger comparative evidence, seven-benchmark generalization tests, contamination checks and detailed training and annotation instructions. These substantially address attribution and reproducibility gaps. Numerical inconsistencies, such as Table 6 versus its discussion, and the unexplained binary-versus-ternary PRM labels in Equation 2 and Appendix A.3 weaken precision, but the stronger empirical support and documentation provide a clear substantial net improvement.
